title: Paused lock holder
description: A nightly ledger job takes a lease-based lock with a 30-second TTL from a coordination service before writing balance adjustments to the ledger database. One night the worker holding the lock hits a 45-second garbage-collection pause; another worker acquires the lock and starts the job. When the first worker resumes it continues writing, and some adjustments are applied twice. What change prevents this?

options.text: Increase the lease TTL to 5 minutes so pauses never outlast it
options.explanation: Any TTL can be exceeded by a long enough pause, and a longer TTL also delays recovery when the holder genuinely dies.

options.text: Issue a monotonically increasing fencing token with each lease and have the ledger database reject writes carrying a token lower than the highest it has accepted
options.explanation: The resource itself enforces ordering of lock holders, so the resumed worker's stale token is rejected regardless of how long it was paused.

options.text: Have the worker check the system clock before each write and stop if more than 30 seconds have passed since acquiring the lock
options.explanation: The pause can happen between the check and the write, and wall clocks can jump, so the check gives no guarantee.

options.text: Run the coordination service on 4 nodes instead of 3 for higher availability
options.explanation: A 4-node cluster still tolerates only one failure and does nothing about a client that does not know its lease expired.
